title: Commercial Shipping – Who’s Who
description: Learn about the main parties involved in commercial shipping, including shipowners, charterers, ship managers, brokers, agents, insurers, surveyors, freight forwarders and cargo interests.

questions.question: Which party has legal ownership of a merchant vessel?
questions.explanation: The shipowner legally owns the vessel and is ultimately responsible for ensuring that it is registered, insured, maintained and operated in accordance with applicable requirements.

questions.question: Who is the consignee in a cargo shipment?
options: The party that receives the cargo
The company that technically manages the vessel
The insurer covering the vessel's machinery
questions.explanation: The consignee is the party named to receive the cargo at its destination.

questions.question: Which party normally sends the cargo and arranges for it to enter the transport chain?
questions.explanation: The shipper is the party that sends or presents the cargo for transportation.

questions.question: What is the main role of a freight forwarder?
options: To classify and certify merchant ships
To coordinate cargo transportation and logistics
To command the vessel during a voyage
To own all vessels used in the transport chain
questions.explanation: A freight forwarder coordinates the movement of goods from origin to destination, which may include shipping, warehousing, customs clearance and inland transportation.

questions.question: Which party is hired to use a vessel for a voyage or a specified period?
questions.explanation: A charterer hires the use of a vessel under an agreed charterparty, either for a voyage, a period of time or under a bareboat arrangement.

questions.question: What is the main function of a ship broker?
options: To recruit and train the vessel's crew
To inspect machinery after an accident
To connect shipowners and charterers and assist with negotiations
To arrange medical treatment for seafarers
questions.explanation: A ship broker acts as a professional intermediary, connecting shipowners and charterers and helping negotiate freight rates, hire, terms and contracts.

questions.question: Which party normally coordinates pilotage, towage, berth arrangements and port documentation for a vessel call?
questions.explanation: A port or ship agent represents the owner or charterer locally and coordinates the practical requirements of the vessel's port call.

questions.question: What does a crewing agent primarily do?
options: Negotiates the sale and purchase of vessels
Recruits seafarers and arranges contracts, travel and training
questions.explanation: A crewing agent recruits and arranges personnel for vessels and helps ensure that the crew meet regulatory and operational requirements.

questions.question: Which type of marine insurance mainly covers physical damage to the ship and its machinery?
questions.explanation: Hull and Machinery insurance normally covers physical loss of or damage to the insured vessel, including its hull and machinery, subject to the policy terms.

questions.question: Which organisation commonly covers liabilities such as cargo claims, crew injuries, pollution and certain fines?
questions.explanation: Protection and Indemnity clubs provide mutual liability insurance for risks that are generally not covered by standard Hull and Machinery insurance.

questions.question: A company hires a vessel for one cargo movement from Brazil to China. Which charter arrangement is most likely?
questions.explanation: A voyage charterer hires a vessel for a specific voyage between agreed loading and discharge locations.

questions.question: A company hires a vessel for twelve months, directs its commercial voyages and normally pays for bunkers and port charges. What type of charterer is it?
questions.explanation: Under a time charter, the charterer uses the vessel for an agreed period and normally pays voyage-related costs such as bunkers and port charges.

questions.question: A company takes over a vessel without crew or provisions and assumes extensive operational control. Which arrangement does this describe?
questions.explanation: A bareboat charterer leases the vessel without crew or provisions and assumes a level of control and responsibility similar to that of an owner for the charter period.

questions.question: A shipowner outsources budgeting, maintenance planning, regulatory compliance and day-to-day technical operation. Which party would normally perform these duties?
questions.explanation: A ship manager acts on behalf of the shipowner and may oversee technical operations, maintenance, compliance, budgeting and coordination with maritime stakeholders.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a shipowner from a ship manager?
options: The manager owns the cargo, while the owner arranges customs clearance
The owner legally owns the vessel, while the manager may operate it on the owner's behalf
The manager always charters the vessel, while the owner acts as port agent
The owner inspects cargo, while the manager provides marine insurance
questions.explanation: Ownership and management can be separated. The owner retains legal ownership, while a contracted ship manager may handle the vessel's day-to-day technical and administrative operation.

questions.question: A scheduled container shipping company needs a local representative to handle cargo bookings, issue bills of lading, assist customers and coordinate berth scheduling. Who should it appoint?
questions.explanation: A liner agent represents a shipping line and may handle bookings, bills of lading, customer contact, customs documentation and port coordination.

questions.question: Following cargo damage, an independent professional is appointed to inspect the goods, establish their condition and issue a factual report. Who is this?
questions.explanation: A marine or cargo surveyor inspects ships or cargo and reports on condition, damage, quality, quantity, value or compliance.

questions.question: A dispute arises over charterparty terms, cargo liability, salvage and general average. Which specialist is most likely to advise the parties?
questions.explanation: Maritime lawyers specialise in legal matters such as charterparties, cargo claims, collision, salvage, insurance, pollution and general average.

questions.question: A business buys grain internationally and contracts shipping services to deliver it to overseas buyers. Which commercial role best describes the business?
questions.explanation: A trader buys and sells commodities such as grain, oil or metals and may contract vessels or other transport services to move those commodities.

questions.question: Which sequence most accurately represents a simple cargo movement while distinguishing the cargo interests from the carrier?
options: Port Agent → Ship Manager → P&I Club
questions.explanation: In a simplified cargo chain, the shipper sends the goods, the carrier transports them and the consignee receives them.
